email.subject: Case 7731: a card payment we blocked

body.v: We blocked a card payment of CHF 389.00 at an online shop. To close the case we need to confirm that it was you who stopped it.
In a moment you will receive a six-digit code by text message. Please reply to this email with that code and we will finish the case.

hotspots.explain: swissalpbank-desk.example is not the bank's domain, swissalpbank.example.
No deadline and no threat. The tone is calm and helpful, which is why it works.
A code sent to your phone is a key. A real bank never asks you to read it back or reply with it. With it, the sender can approve their own payment.
The case page is on the lookalike domain.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be the bank's fraud desk. The address is on swissalpbank-desk.example, not swissalpbank.example.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Little pressure here: authority and helpfulness. The calm tone makes you want to cooperate.
choices: Authority and a wish to help

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Reply with the code that arrives on your phone. That code approves a transaction or a login for the sender.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Hand over a code sent to your phone

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not reply. Call the number on the back of your card, or open the SwissAlpBank app yourself, and ask about case 7731.
choices: Reply with the code to close the case
View the case on the page they give you
Call the number on the back of your card

actions.label: Call the number on the back of your card and ask about the case
actions.consequence: The bank knows nothing about case 7731. The email was fake.

actions.label: Reply with the code when it arrives
actions.consequence: The sender uses your code to approve a payment or log in as you.

actions.label: View the case on the page they give you
actions.consequence: The page asks for your login and card details. Both go to the scammer.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. You gave nothing away.

attacker_reveal: No rush, no threats, a case number and a friendly name... I only wanted six digits from your phone. A real bank never asks you to read a code back to anyone.
